title: Simulated-impact runway and approval mesh for incremental batching & KV-cache launches
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a safe, auditable path to automatically apply cost-saving batching and KV-cache recommendations by combining preflight simulation ('SimRun'), an approval mesh that routes sign-offs, and progressive activation gates. The goal is to reduce manual toil for low-risk recommendations while keeping human oversight and automated rollback for unexpected latency or quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: SimRun can replay representative traffic for a target config and produce a deterministic delta report (cost delta, p50/p95 latency, errors per 1k, token throughput, quality regression score) within 30 minutes for a single model+route pair.
Approval mesh allows role-based signoff flows: auto-approve (for <1% latency increase and >3% cost reduction), ops-approval, and executive-approval tiers configurable per-customer cohort.
Canary protocol enforces staged activation across 5 cohorts (shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if telemetry crosses thresholds for SLO degradation or quality regressions.
All activations produce an immutable audit artifact with pre/post diffs, the SimRun report, sign-offs (user IDs), and a rollback plan link.
Integration tests covering end-to-end apply -> canary rollout -> automatic rollback are added to CI and passing in the staging environment.
implementation_notes: Component 1 - SimRun: a controller that clones recent request traces and runs them through a candidate config in an isolated sandbox to measure deterministic deltas. Use sampled production traffic (1-5%) and synthetic edge cases to detect regressions.

Component 2 - Delta Scoring: compute multi-dimensional score (cost, latency, error-rate, hallucination proxy) and map to risk buckets (low/medium/high). Store artifacts in S3 and index summaries in telemetry store.
Component 3 - Approval Mesh: extensible workflow engine to route approvals based on team, customer tier, and delta score. Supports auto-approve rules and manual handoff to oncall.
Component 4 - Canary Enactor: staged activation engine integrated with routing layer. Cohorts defined by customer tags/regions; supports immediate kill switch and rollback hooks.
Component 5 - Observability and Alerts: per-cohort dashboards, pre-defined CanaryGuard thresholds, and auto-generated Runbook snippets for oncall.

Note: strive for non-blocking UX for trivial low-risk recommendations (e.g., quantization-only, no expected latency impact) while requiring operator escrow for anything that touches production routing or KV cache semantics.
risks: SimRun may not capture user-perceived quality regressions (requires robust hallucination proxy and regression tests).
False negatives in sampling could let a problematic config reach broader cohorts—mitigate with conservative default thresholds and extended shadow runs for first-time model families.
Approval mesh complexity adds operational overhead; needs clear defaults and templates to avoid unnecessary friction for engineers.
Rollback paths must be well-tested; ambiguous rollback states across multi-variant requests (model family fallback) are tricky.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SimRun simulator and deterministic replay harness.
E2E test in staging that runs a representative 10k request bundle through current config vs candidate and validates delta report generation.
Chaos tests: simulate slow kernels and memory pressure during canary to ensure rollback triggers correctly.
Pilot with internal customers (two product teams) before broad rollout. Collect qualitative feedback on false positives/negatives from PM/DS.
implementation_timeline: Week 1: Prototype SimRun harness and deterministic replay for a single model-route pair.
Week 2: Wire Delta Scoring and store artifacts; produce initial delta report UI in Console (read-only).
Week 3: Build Approval Mesh with two flow types (auto and ops-approve).
Week 4: Canary Enactor integration and basic rollback hooks; internal pilot with two teams.
Week 5: Add observability dashboards, chaos tests, and finalize runbook.
Week 6: Gradual rollout and retro; collect metrics and iterate on thresholds.
